name: UPSC

levels.note: Any degree. Age 21–32 (relaxations: SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC 3 yrs). 6 attempts (General).
B.E./B.Tech in relevant branch. Age 21–30 (IES). 6 attempts.

stages.name: Preliminary Exam
stages.tests: Paper 1: GS (100 Qs, 200 marks, 2 hrs). Paper 2: CSAT (80 Qs, 200 marks, 2 hrs).
stages.note: CSAT qualifying (33%). GS score decides cut-off. Negative marking 1/3.

stages.name: Main Exam
stages.tests: 9 papers: Essay, GS I-IV, Optional I-II, Language (qualifying). Total 1750 marks.
stages.note: Written. 3 hrs per paper. Optional subject chosen by candidate.

stages.name: Personality Test (Interview)
stages.tests: 275 marks. Board of 4-5 members. 30-45 min. Personality, current affairs, optional subject.
stages.note: No coaching can substitute genuine personality. DAF (Detailed Application Form) is key.

stages.name: Final Merit
stages.tests: Mains (1750) + Interview (275) = 2025 marks. Service allocated by rank + preference.
stages.note: Top 900-1000 candidates recommended. Service allocation by merit + preference.

reality: UPSC CSE is the most competitive exam in India. 10 lakh+ applicants, ~900 vacancies. Success rate < 0.1%.
Preparation takes 1-2 years minimum. Many take 3-4 attempts. Average age of successful candidate: 27-28.
Optional subject choice is crucial. Choose based on interest and scoring potential, not popularity.
Current affairs matter more than static knowledge. Read The Hindu/Indian Express daily.
Interview is not about knowledge — it tests personality, balance, and integrity. DAF preparation is key.
Service allocation: IAS > IPS > IFS > IRS (by rank). Top 100 get IAS. Rank 100-200 get IPS/IFS.

faq.q: How many attempts are allowed for UPSC CSE?
faq.a: General: 6 attempts (age 21-32). OBC: 9 attempts (age 21-35). SC/ST: unlimited (age 21-37). PwD: 9 attempts (age 21-42).

faq.q: What is the difference between IAS and IPS?
faq.a: IAS = administrative service (district collector, policy making). IPS = police service (SP, DIG, DGP). Both are Group A. IAS has higher status and broader scope.

faq.q: Can I choose my optional subject freely?
faq.a: Yes. Any subject from the UPSC list. No restriction based on graduation. Choose based on interest, syllabus overlap with GS, and availability of study material.

faq.q: What is the UPSC interview like?
faq.a: 275 marks. 4-5 member board. 30-45 minutes. Questions on DAF (hobbies, education, work), current affairs, optional subject, and situational judgment. No right/wrong answers — personality assessment.
Not mandatory. Many clear without coaching. Coaching helps with structure and mock tests. Self-study with standard books + test series is equally effective.

faq.q: Where do I find official UPSC notifications?
faq.a: upsc.gov.in (main site) and upsconline.nic.in (application). SarkariJobs+ links the official notification PDF on every listing page.
